name: Bibblino Scrollino
chant: Bibblino Scrollino! Bibblino Scrollino! Lampada ai miei piedi, luce sul mio cammino!

passages.text: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
I have hidden Your word in my heart that I might not sin against You.

All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness, so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.
For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

name: Jonahrino Whalerino
chant: Jonahrino Whalerino! Jonahrino Whalerino! Inghiottito dal pescione, tre giorni nel pancione!

passages.text: Now the LORD had appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish.

Jonah, however, got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish. So he paid the fare and went aboard to sail for Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.
And the LORD commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.
When God saw their actions—that they had turned from their evil ways—He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them.

name: Samsonini Jawbonini
chant: Samsonini Jawbonini! Samsonini Jawbonini! Con la mascella d'asino, mille nemici giù!

passages.text: He found the fresh jawbone of a donkey, reached out his hand and took it, and struck down a thousand men. Then Samson said: “With the jawbone of a donkey I have piled them into heaps. With the jawbone of a donkey I have slain a thousand men.”

But Samson lay there only until midnight, when he got up, took hold of the doors of the city gate and both gateposts, and pulled them out, bar and all. Then he put them on his shoulders and took them to the top of the mountain overlooking Hebron.

Samson told her all that was in his heart: “My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb. If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, and I will become as weak as any other man.”

And Samson reached out for the two central pillars supporting the temple. Bracing himself against them with his right hand on one pillar and his left hand on the other, Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines.” Then he pushed with all his might, and the temple fell on the lords and all the people in it. So in his death he killed more than he had killed in his life.

name: Donkino Talkino
chant: Donkino Talkino! L'asina parla, il profeta non capisce niente!

passages.text: Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”
But the donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not the donkey you have ridden all your life until today? Have I ever treated you this way before?” “No,” he replied.
Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. And Balaam bowed low and fell facedown.

name: Goliatho Bonkatello
chant: Goliatho Bonkatello! Grande grande grande, un sassolino in fronte, bum! Giù per terra!

passages.text: Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out from the Philistine camp. He was six cubits and a span in height,

But David said to the Philistine, “You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
Then David reached into his bag, took out a stone, and slung it, striking the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell facedown on the ground.
Thus David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; without a sword in his hand he struck down the Philistine and killed him.

name: Baldini Bearini
chant: Baldini Bearini! Non chiamarlo testa pelata, arrivano due orse!

passages.text: From there, Elisha went up to Bethel, and as he was walking up the road, a group of boys came out of the city and jeered at him, chanting, “Go up, you baldhead! Go up, you baldhead!” Then he turned around, looked at them, and called down a curse on them in the name of the LORD. Suddenly two female bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the boys.

As one of them was cutting down a tree, the iron axe head fell into the water. “Oh, my master,” he cried out, “it was borrowed!” “Where did it fall?” asked the man of God. And when he showed him the place, the man of God cut a stick, threw it there, and made the iron float.

name: Elijahtti Chariotti
chant: Elijahtti Chariotti! Carro di fuoco, cavalli di fuoco, vrum vrum, dritto in cielo!

passages.text: As they were walking along and talking together, suddenly a chariot of fire with horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them, and Elijah went up into heaven in a whirlwind.
At noon Elijah began to taunt them, saying, “Shout louder, for he is a god! Perhaps he is deep in thought, or occupied, or on a journey. Perhaps he is sleeping and must be awakened!”
Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and it licked up the water in the trench.

name: Moobuchadnezzar Grassolini
chant: Moobuchadnezzar Grassolini! Re di Babilonia, mangia l'erba come un bue!

passages.text: At that moment the sentence against Nebuchadnezzar was fulfilled. He was driven away from mankind. He ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like the feathers of an eagle and his nails like the claws of a bird.

But at the end of those days I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven, and my sanity was restored to me. Then I praised the Most High, and I honored and glorified Him who lives forever: “For His dominion is an everlasting dominion, and His kingdom endures from generation to generation.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, for all His works are true and all His ways are just. And He is able to humble those who walk in pride.

name: Lionini Napini
chant: Lionini Napini! Daniele nella fossa, ma l'angelo chiude la bocca ai leoni!

passages.text: So the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions. The king said to Daniel, “May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you!”
My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions. They have not hurt me, for I was found innocent in His sight, and I have done no wrong against you, O king.”
The king was overjoyed and gave orders to lift Daniel out of the den, and when Daniel was lifted out of the den, no wounds whatsoever were found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

name: Froggo Pharaoggo
chant: Froggo Pharaoggo! Rane nel letto, rane nel forno, rane dappertutto! Cra cra cra!

passages.text: The Nile will teem with frogs, and they will come into your palace and up to your bedroom and onto your bed, into the houses of your officials and your people, and into your ovens and kneading bowls.
So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
And the LORD did as Moses requested, and the frogs in the houses, the courtyards, and the fields died. They were piled into countless heaps, and there was a terrible stench in the land.

name: Methuselino Oldissimo
chant: Methuselino Oldissimo! Novecentosessantanove anni, troppe candeline!

passages.text: So Methuselah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died.

When Enoch was 65 years old, he became the father of Methuselah. And after he had become the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked with God 300 years and had other sons and daughters. So Enoch lived a total of 365 years. Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.

name: Leviathan Linguini
chant: Leviathan Linguini! Fuoco dalla bocca, fumo dal naso, il mare bolle come una pentola!

passages.text: “Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?
Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth! Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds. His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames pour from his mouth.
He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.

name: Shortino Sycamorino
chant: Shortino Sycamorino! Piccolo piccolino, sale sul sicomoro per vedere Gesù!

passages.text: He was trying to see who Jesus was, but could not see over the crowd because he was small in stature. So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Him, since Jesus was about to pass that way.
When Jesus came to that place, He looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.”
But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.”

name: Snoozino Windowino
chant: Snoozino Windowino! Paolo predica, predica, predica, lui dorme e cade dalla finestra!

passages.text: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.
But Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and embraced him. “Do not be alarmed!” he said. “He is still alive!”
And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive.

name: Peterino Sinkerino
chant: Peterino Sinkerino! Cammina sull'acqua, guarda il vento, glu glu glu!

passages.text: “Come,” said Jesus. Then Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.
But when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid and, beginning to sink, cried out, “Lord, save me!”
Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter. “You of little faith,” He said, “why did you doubt?”

name: Noahzino Arkarino
chant: Noahzino Arkarino! Animali a due a due, piove per quaranta giorni!

passages.text: came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.
And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
And behold, the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak. So Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.

name: Mosessino Seasplittino
chant: Mosessino Seasplittino! Alza il bastone, e il mare si apre in due!

passages.text: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind that turned it into dry land. So the waters were divided,
and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.
The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen—the entire army of Pharaoh that had chased the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.

name: Saltina Lookbackina
chant: Saltina Lookbackina! Non guardare indietro... troppo tardi, è sale!

passages.text: But Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
As soon as the men had brought them out, one of them said, “Run for your lives! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere on the plain! Flee to the mountains, or you will be swept away!”
Remember Lot’s wife!

name: Jacobino Ladderino
chant: Jacobino Ladderino! Dorme su una pietra, angeli su e giù per la scala!

passages.text: On reaching a certain place, he spent the night there because the sun had set. And taking one of the stones from that place, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep. And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven, and God’s angels were going up and down the ladder.
When Jacob woke up, he said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was unaware of it.”
So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.

name: Josephino Coatcolorino
chant: Josephino Coatcolorino! Tunica colorata, buttato nel pozzo, poi capo d'Egitto!

passages.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons, because Joseph had been born to him in his old age; so he made him a robe of many colors.
So when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped him of his robe—the robe of many colors he was wearing— and they took him and threw him into the pit. Now the pit was empty, with no water in it.
Pharaoh also told Joseph, “I hereby place you over all the land of Egypt.”
As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good, in order to accomplish a day like this—to preserve the lives of many people.

name: Jerichino Wallcrashino
chant: Jerichino Wallcrashino! Sette giri, trombe e grida, e le mura crollano!

passages.text: Then on the seventh day, they got up at dawn and marched around the city seven times in the same manner. That was the only day they circled the city seven times. After the seventh time around, the priests blew the horns, and Joshua commanded the people, “Shout! For the LORD has given you the city!

So when the rams’ horns sounded, the people shouted. When they heard the blast of the horn, the people gave a great shout, and the wall collapsed. Then all the people charged straight into the city and captured it.

name: Raveno Deliverino
chant: Raveno Deliverino! Consegna a domicilio: pane e carne, mattina e sera!

passages.text: And you are to drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”
The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he would drink from the brook.

name: Furnacino Chillino
chant: Furnacino Chillino! Fornace sette volte più calda, ma nemmeno l'odore del fuoco!

passages.text: If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king. But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.”
At this, Nebuchadnezzar was filled with rage, and the expression on his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He gave orders to heat the furnace seven times hotter than usual,

and when the satraps, prefects, governors, and royal advisers had gathered around, they saw that the fire had no effect on the bodies of these men. Not a hair of their heads was singed, their robes were unaffected, and there was no smell of fire on them.

name: Babelino Towerino
chant: Babelino Towerino! Una torre fino al cielo, poi tutti parlano lingue diverse!

passages.text: “Come,” they said, “let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.”
Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.”
That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world, and from that place the LORD scattered them over the face of all the earth.

name: Lazzarino Wakeupino
chant: Lazzarino Wakeupino! Quattro giorni nella tomba, poi esce fuori tutto bendato!

passages.text: “Take away the stone,” Jesus said. “Lord, by now he stinks,” said Martha, the sister of the dead man. “It has already been four days.”

After Jesus had said this, He called out in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!” The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen, and his face wrapped in a cloth. “Unwrap him and let him go,” Jesus told them.

name: Breadino Fishino
chant: Breadino Fishino! Cinque pani, due pesci, cinquemila persone sazie!

passages.text: “Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish. But what difference will these make among so many?”
Then Jesus took the loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted.
So they collected them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten.

name: Skeletrino Rattlerino
chant: Skeletrino Rattlerino! Ossa secche, clack clack clack, tornano in vita!

passages.text: And He said to me, “Prophesy concerning these bones and tell them, ‘Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD!
So I prophesied as I had been commanded. And as I prophesied, there was suddenly a noise, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to bone.
So I prophesied as He had commanded me, and the breath entered them, and they came to life and stood on their feet—a vast army.

name: Prodigalino Piggerino
chant: Prodigalino Piggerino! Spende tutto, vuole il cibo dei maiali, poi torna dal papà!

passages.text: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.
He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.
So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.

name: Paulino Snakeshakino
chant: Paulino Snakeshakino! La vipera lo morde, lui la scuote nel fuoco, niente!

passages.text: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.

But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects. The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

name: Davidino Dancerino
chant: Davidino Dancerino! Balla davanti al Signore con tutte le sue forze!

passages.text: And David, wearing a linen ephod, danced with all his might before the LORD,
while he and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and the sounding of the ram’s horn.
